label: Integument
description:
“The body is our general medium for having a world.”
- Maurice Merleau-Ponty, Phenomenology of Perception

If the body is the medium through which the world is perceived and experienced, what happens when that world loses its coherence?

Adaptive Flesh is an ongoing research project exploring body architectures as both aesthetic and functional systems of adaptation.

Drawing from the idea of forced evolution, this research imagines bodies pushed beyond their natural limits, becoming enhanced organisms capable of adapting to conditions they were never meant to inhabit.

At the core of this project is the idea of the threshold: the moment in which one state begins to rupture into another. This is represented via a visual system of "processes" through which surfaces are opened and redesigned.
